title: Positivity of $\lfloor np\rfloor$ for large $n$
statement: Let $p$ be a real number with $0 < p$ and $0 < 1 - p$, and set $N_2 = \lceil 2/(p(1-p))\rceil + 1$. Then for every natural number $n$ with $N_2 \le n$, the floor $\lfloor np\rfloor$ is strictly positive, i.e. $\lfloor np\rfloor \ge 1$.
replaced: Let $0<p$ and $0<1-p$, and set $N_2 = \lceil 2/(p(1-p))\rceil + 1$. If $N_2 \le n$, then $\lfloor np\rfloor > 0$.
